summary: Prevention encodes the hindered participant with a person suffix, while m- can introduce the blocked activity (24/177); the room in 57/73 is instead an ʕal-marked domain.
manəʕ with kit/layt is likely nominal 'prohibition/objection', but the entry explicitly files it under Part act.; new parallel examples follow that inherited convention rather than rewriting it.
The Arabic-pattern mamnuʕ predicates are useful contact evidence, including an impersonal d-clause. Their existence does not prove productive II Detransitive Part. Pass. morphology.

II.2 food restriction, non-reflexive wasting and Detransitive wasting are related in the current entry but differ in argument coding. The rank-renunciation verse reveals why reflexive abstention must be explicit in the active gloss.
The existing Detransitive boxes already have label 2; an explicit list item repairs the parsed structural gap. No existing example is renumbered.
III Infectum-wa in the counterfactual reasoning at 57/73 extends the attested form inventory without adding a new meaning.
Jan's English is project machine translation, copied only as supplied and not used to establish senses. All interpretations were checked against the Turoyo.
Contracted mnəʕ- adds II Infectum and Preterit-wa; III mamnəʕile adds Preterit. -wo plus l-agent segmentation remains provisional.
Learned mniʕo/mniʕe is predicative and attributive, with mi ḥkume in one clause. The narrow learned prohibition result does not establish productive spoken morphology. Arabic mamnuʕ remains distinct.
Governments prohibit products or activities; u ʕamo can be the restricted object. -la in mnəʕwola refers contextually to the government.
Should lexical mamnuʕ be cross-referenced as an Arabic adjective, and is any productive Turoyo participial paradigm independently attested?
Should existential manəʕ remain under the inherited Part act. convention, or receive a noun cross-reference? No inherited example is moved on this evidence.
At 66/71 does (+det) mark a semantic observation, or should the surface manaʕle be corrected from the original edition? No silent replacement is made.
Does II.2 comprise both intransitive wasting and a conventional reflexive abstention construction? The proposed gloss explicitly preserves both.
Confirm mnəʕwo-la/-le/-lle and mamnəʕile vocalism.
Is learned mniʕo/mniʕe integrated II Detransitive Part. Pass. or a lexical Syriac adjective? Productive morphology is not assumed.
Does abstinent mniʕo at Jan 2.16/3557 share that paradigm? No new Detransitive abstention sense is proposed.
Check monəʕ/kmənaʕlan vocalism and the cemetery prohibition's exact scope.
